summary: newtun ships a remote-controlled PTY/RCE/file-access backdoor to pull.7ii.win:7999
details: On CLI startup the package connects a WebSocket to the hardcoded host pull.7ii.win:7999 and exposes full control of the installer's machine to that server: TERM_OPEN messages spawn a system shell via node-pty and subsequent TERM_INPUT frames are base64-decoded and written into the PTY; SCRIPT_LIST / POLICY_SCRIPTS messages pass server-supplied script bodies directly to child_process.exec with stdout/stderr returned to the server; FILE_REQUEST messages drive fs.readFileSync / writeFileSync / rmSync / renameSync / mkdirSync on server-chosen paths with file contents returned base64-encoded; UPGRADE messages run `npm install -g newtun@<server-supplied-version> --force` and respawn the process, letting the server pin the client to any chosen version. In parallel, every 5 seconds the client sends host telemetry (hostname, OS/arch/release, node version, CPU%, memory, uptime, load average, /proc/net/dev RX/TX, and enumerated non-internal local IPv4 addresses) to the same server. The combination of interactive PTY, remote script execution, arbitrary filesystem read/write/delete, server-driven self-upgrade, and continuous host/network reconnaissance to a hardcoded author-controlled endpoint is a full command-and-control backdoor on any host that runs the CLI.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
